edbDesc: A free falling object achieves its terminal velocity when the downward force of gravity equals the upward force of drag. This causes the net force on the object to be zero, resulting in an acceleration of zero. Mathematically an object asymptotically approaches and can never reach its terminal velocity.
title: Terminal Velocity
pickWhy: A generic mechanics result (drag balancing gravity), not a specific effect; the deck's falling-motion card touches on air resistance.
